anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Quoted sense: the letter kills, the Spirit makes alive.
Eating the flesh for life, not death.

choices.why: The words without the Spirit — the same psilos as in 1.1's 'name taken simply'.

pass_a_gloss: If then some use the bare words themselves, these would chew the Savior's fleshes raw, and partaking of his fleshes raw they will procure death for themselves and not life, eating his fleshes beastlike and not humanly, since the letter to kill, but the Spirit to make alive, the apostle teaches us.
pass_b_english: If then some use the bare words themselves, these would be chewing the flesh of the Savior raw. And partaking of his flesh raw they will procure death for themselves and not life, eating his flesh in a beastlike way and not as humans — since the apostle teaches us that the letter kills, but the Spirit makes alive (2 Corinthians 3:6) (John 6:53–54).
